Read an item bank

Source: R/fct_item_bank.R
read_item_bank.Rd

Reads the item bank of a questionnaire, fitted with the rating scale model of mirt (itemtype = "rsm"), and converts the coefficients to the form of the engine (Pi_rsm): \(\lambda_j = -c\) and \(\delta_t = b_t\). It stops with a message naming the problem when the file is not a complete rating scale bank, so that an app does not start and then fail on the first answer.

read_item_bank(items_csv)

Arguments

items_csv

Path to the csv file, saved as UTF-8.

Value

A data frame, one row per item: scale, question, stem, reverse, lambdaj, delta1 to delta4, prior_mean (always 0) and prior_sd.

Details

The csv has one row per item, with the columns scale and question (the text of the item); a1, b1 to b4 and c, the coefficients of mirt; and prior_sd, the standard deviation of the latent distribution of the scale, which mirt estimates. Optional columns: stem, the instruction shown above the item, and reverse (TRUE/FALSE), for items whose answers were reversed (6 - answer) before the fit. Other columns are ignored.

See also

Other item bank: ipip50(), read_likert(), validate_item_bank_against_mirt()

Examples

bank <- read_item_bank(system.file("extdata", "ipip50_items.csv", package = "golemcat"))
head(bank[, c("scale", "question", "reverse", "lambdaj")])
#>           scale                                        question reverse
#> 1 Agreeableness                     I Make people feel at ease.   FALSE
#> 2 Agreeableness               I Feel little concern for others.    TRUE
#> 3 Agreeableness                      I Am interested in people.   FALSE
#> 4 Agreeableness                                I Insult people.    TRUE
#> 5 Agreeableness             I Sympathize with others' feelings.   FALSE
#> 6 Agreeableness I Am not interested in other people's problems.    TRUE
#>        lambdaj
#> 1  0.005745269
#> 2  0.000000000
#> 3 -0.276373167
#> 4 -0.168629507
#> 5 -0.408719449
#> 6 -0.164829510
